sources.title: Ember-1 API & Playground
sources.evidence: Exact Ember-1 page lists 2.78T parameters, MoE, image input and function calling; context is displayed as 1040k. Its September 22 date is creation metadata. Fresh October 27 read confirms the exact model still reports 2.78T and explicitly says it is built on Kimi K3. This supports the nominal total independently of any tensor census.

sources.title: Introducing Ember-1
sources.evidence: September 23, 2026 launch says available today, identifies Fireworks Research and the Ember series, and describes a Kimi K3 derivative trained for shorter reasoning. Release is a hosted research preview. Fresh October 27 read confirms explicit named-base lineage: Fireworks trained Kimi K3 on task/environment feedback to shorten reasoning traces, and calls Ember-1 a version of K3. No pruning, smaller student, expert expansion, changed routing or new modality is described. The reduced token count is a learned generation behavior, not a claim of fewer weights.

sources.title: Vercel AI Gateway live model metadata
sources.evidence: The exact fireworks/ember-1 object reports context_window 1048576, text/image input, text output, reasoning and tool-use tags. JSON was retrieved directly and saved under /tmp/model-audit-186/vercel-models.json.

sources.title: Ember-1 (Fireworks) - Cloudflare AI documentation
sources.evidence: Cloudflare documents 1,040,000 context tokens, text generation and function calling for Ember-1, and links to Fireworks terms. This differs from the Vercel route metadata.

sources.title: Fireworks Terms of Service, July 10, 2026
sources.evidence: The official link redirects to a PDF, retrieved with curl and extracted with pdftotext after the web tool failed. Sections 2 and 7 limit service access and reserve Fireworks ownership; no open-weight license is granted.

sources.title: Kimi K3 on Fireworks: Fast RL at frontier scale
sources.evidence: Fresh October 27 direct retrieval succeeded after the web reader failed. Independently inspected the complete October 12 systems report, including parameter, architecture and training sections. It describes full-parameter and LoRA training on Kimi K3 at 2.8T, with 896 routed experts/top-16 and the existing hybrid attention. The report supplies context for Fireworks K3 training rather than an Ember-specific count; no structural compression is described. The separate Ember launch establishes the exact derivative relationship.

sources.title: Can open models carry readable silent signals before they speak?
sources.evidence: August 12, 2026 interpretability report was retrieved directly. It studies Kimi K3 and Qwen3.5-9B; it does not establish additional Ember-1 architecture or parameter specifications.

sources.title: LAB leaderboard by Harvey - Fireworks Specialized Intelligence Index
sources.evidence: October 20, 2026 first-party comparison distinguishes Fireworks Ember-1 from Moonshot Kimi K3. It provides evaluations and serving methodology, not an Ember active-parameter count. Fresh October 27 complete retrieval and comparison-heading/parameter search found no additional active-count disclosure or architecture change. Benchmark differentiation does not contradict the declared K3 training lineage.

sources.title: Ember-1 API, Pricing & Playground
sources.evidence: Official serving-provider page identifies the Ember-1 research preview, image input, function calling, Fireworks legal terms and September 23 release date.

sources.title: Kimi K3 official model card
sources.evidence: Fresh October 27 read of the official card, including raw README to inspect the architecture table, confirms 2.8T total and 104B activated parameters. This is the explicitly named base of Ember-1. The rounded nominal active count is inherited through Fireworks documented post-training relationship, not independently measured for Ember.

sources.title: Kimi K3: Open Frontier Intelligence
sources.evidence: Fresh October 27 full-report retrieval and independent inspection of Table 1 confirms the base model has 2.78T total and 104.2B activated parameters, with 896 routed experts, 16 selected and 2 shared experts. Its abstract/card use rounded 2.8T/104B. Preserve Fireworks own 2.78T total and use the supported rounded 104B convention for the derivative; this is a labeled nominal lineage inference rather than an exact hosted-checkpoint census.

name.note: Exact public model name and endpoint match the assigned record.

developer.note: Fireworks identifies this as its own model, developed by Fireworks Research.

family.note: Normalized label for the explicitly named Ember model series; Kimi K3 is the underlying model, not the product family.

release_date.note: The dated launch explicitly announces availability that day. September 22 on the model page is labeled Created on and does not establish public release. Later gateway listings are not the first release.

open_weights.note: The documented release provides hosted research-preview access under Fireworks terms. No public Ember-1 checkpoint or weight-download license was identified in the official release, model page or targeted first-party/Hugging Face searches; base-model openness does not establish derivative availability.

license.note: Descriptive classification of hosted access under Fireworks commercial service terms, not an SPDX weight license. No open license for the Ember-1 derivative is documented.

parameters_b.note: Fresh exact-model page confirms Fireworks nominal 2.78T total, or 2780B, consistent with the named Kimi K3 base report. Preserve the vendor-published precision; no tensor census is required.

active_parameters_b.note: Nominal 104B activated parameters, inferred from Fireworks explicit post-training of Kimi K3 and Moonshot’s official 104B specification. Fresh exact-model searches and original/later primary sources describe shortening generated reasoning through training, with no disclosed pruning, smaller student, expert expansion or modality change. K3 Table 1 reports a finer 104.2B; the rounded card convention is retained for this hosted derivative, not asserted as an exact Ember tensor count.

architecture.note: The Ember page explicitly confirms mixture-of-experts. More specific hybrid-attention structure is documented for Kimi K3; it is not asserted for this unreleased checkpoint.

context_window.note: Use the developer-published nominal 1040k limit, represented as 1040000 tokens and corroborated by Cloudflare. Vercel reports 1048576 for its route; this provider difference remains documented rather than replacing the developer limit. No endpoint execution was tested.

modalities.note: Vercel explicitly enumerates these modalities for the exact model; the developer independently confirms image input.

reasoning.note: The release discusses reasoning traces and the live provider metadata exposes reasoning controls.

tool_call.note: Developer lists function calling as supported; exact provider metadata includes tools and tool_choice.

description.value: Fireworks reasoning model based on Kimi K3, trained to shorten reasoning traces for coding and agentic tasks.
description.note: Replaces the unqualified quality claim with a concise purpose and lineage description. Approximately 40% fewer tokens at comparable quality is a developer-reported evaluation result, not a universal performance guarantee.

patch.description: Fireworks reasoning model based on Kimi K3, trained to shorten reasoning traces for coding and agentic tasks.
patch.notes: 2.78T is Fireworks’ nominal total. Nominal 104B active is inferred from its documented post-training of Kimi K3 and the base model’s official specification. Context follows Fireworks’ advertised 1040k tokens (1,040,000), also documented by Cloudflare; Vercel lists 1,048,576 for its route.

sources.label: Vercel AI Gateway live model metadata

summary: October 27 parameter re-audit retains Fireworks nominal 2780B total and recovers nominal 104B active through the explicit Kimi K3 post-training lineage. Fresh exact-model searches, reopened launch/model page, original K3 card/report and later Fireworks training/comparison evidence found no structural change defeating that inference. The prior exact-Ember disclosure requirement was too restrictive for nominal specifications. Added explicit patches and base citations; preserved all unrelated assessments.
